title: Overcoming Disappointment With Resolve
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Built entirely around a single sports anecdote, this piece uses Jalen Hurts’s benching in the January 2018 national championship game as a case study in converting humiliation into effort. Nick Saban pulled his starting quarterback at halftime after 21 passing yards and replaced him with the untested Tua Tagovailova, who threw three touchdown passes to win the title. The essay’s interest is not in Saban’s decision but in what Hurts did on the sideline: hurt and angry, he nonetheless cheered for his replacement and worked to encourage teammates for the remainder of the game. The following morning, before sunrise, he was in the weight room, and spent the following weeks on conditioning and film study. Written on the eve of a Super Bowl five years later, the piece treats that response as a settled disposition rather than a one-off: disappointment is allowed to be felt but never allowed to determine action.
points: The anecdote’s force lies in the gap between internal state and outward conduct — Hurts is described as genuinely hurt and angry while visibly supporting the man who replaced him.
The author marks sleep as the hinge of the story: Hurts did not know how to respond in the moment, so he deferred the response to the next morning rather than reacting badly on the night.
Resolve is defined concretely as redirected effort — weight room and game film — rather than as a mood or an attitude adjustment.
The piece argues that the test of character is whether disappointment is permitted to determine actions, a standard the author says Hurts has held for five years running.
quotes: In January of 2018, as the chance for a fifth national championship was slipping away, Alabama Football Coach Nick Saban faced a difficult choice.
After a disappointing first half with only 21 passing yards, Saban made the executive decision to bench his star quarterback Jalen Hurts and replace him with untested Tua Tagovailova.
During the second half of that game, Jalen Hurts stood on the sideline stunned and disappointed. Being yanked from the game was both a shock and an embarrassment.
But instead of sulking or complaining, Hurts composed himself and cheered voraciously for his replacement.
Before the sun was up, he made a beeline for the team’s weight room and began working on making himself better.
For the next few weeks, he doubled down in the weight room and with game film to take another step forward.
Hurts didn’t let failure or disappointment get in his way or derail his effort to be the best he can be.
